title: Boot-time `npx prisma@5.14.0 db push` replaces the lockfile-integrity-verified prisma CLI with version-tag-only registry resolution, executed at every container boot under the app container's full secret environment
description: Lower-trust actor: whatever registry, mirror, or egress-interposing server answers the boot-time resolution of the version tag `prisma@5.14.0`. Controllable source: the npx handoff itself — version tag only, no lockfile reference, no integrity hash, no offline/prefer-offline flag, no .npmrc, no npm_config_* / NPM_CONFIG_* env, no registry pin anywhere in the repo (repo walk verified), inside a runtime image whose explicit COPY list ships only node_modules/.prisma and never node_modules/prisma or .bin, and an app base/npm implementation itself unbound (node:20-alpine, no @sha256). Consuming trusted process: the compose entrypoint `sh -c "npx prisma@5.14.0 db push && node server.js"` under restart: unless-stopped, which also overrides the Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT so this chain is the only boot process. Consequence: unauthorized code inclusion — whatever the resolution serves runs as node code executing `db push` under DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET, ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD, and NEWSAPI_KEY, against the postgres the same stack trusts. The build stage is calibrated contrast, not mitigation: Dockerfile:6 `npm ci` is the only sha512-bound install (658/658 lockfile resolved entries point to registry.npmjs.org with integrity, re-verified; node_modules/prisma@5.14.0 at package-lock.json:7563/7566) and the runner stage never copies that verified CLI. Refutation paths checked and failed to defeat the trace: no vendored prisma engine (prisma/ holds only schema.prisma and seed.ts), no COPY of the CLI or .bin into the runner, no engines field or overrides in package.json, no .npmrc or npm-config RUN step, no offline knob, no digest-pinned FROM, no repo control that forces a deterministic hard boot failure (no compose read_only/user directive; the toolchain creates the running user's home at Dockerfile:28-29, and npm/npx keep their fetch cache under that home rather than under /app, so a root-owned /app does not reliably abort the fetch). Independently re-produced in-repo fact set: agents/verifier-k/artifacts/observed-verifierk-sweep.json (bounded parent-recipe sandbox, exit 0, static sweep only) and agents/hunter-f/artifacts/observed-t13-lockfile-handoff.json. What remains decisive and outside source/local observation: final-image CLI presence, ambient npm config and writable-cache completability at boot, registry-side content served for the exact tag, and the egress network actor — kept as blockers.
claimed_root_cause: Split resolution root for the same dependency across lifecycle stages: Dockerfile:6 (`npm ci` against package-lock.json copy at :5) binds prisma@5.14.0 by sha512, while docker-compose.yml:39-40 boots `npx prisma@5.14.0 db push` with no lockfile/integrity/offline binding in a runtime image whose COPY list (:32-36) excludes the verified CLI, so every container boot re-opens an unsigned registry resolution slot inside the secret-bearing app container (restart: unless-stopped, :23).

title: Failed-login latency distinguishes registered from unregistered emails (no uniformity control)
description: authorize() performs its membership lookup (prisma.user.findUnique, lib/auth.ts:100-102) before any slow work: unknown emails, rows with null passwordHash, and isActive=false rows exit at lib/auth.ts:104-107 with zero cryptographic work, while a row with a hash always reaches bcrypt.compare (lib/auth.ts:109) against a cost-12 hash (prisma/seed.ts:15; bcryptjs 2.4.3 per package.json:39). Both branches return null, so next-auth answers the same 401 CredentialsSignin body on either path and the only designed distinguisher is wall-clock effort. The surface is pre-auth: the catch-all handler is exported as GET/POST (app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts:6) and the middleware matcher covers only /admin/* and /api/admin/* (middleware.ts:50), not /api/auth. Probe throughput is bounded to 10 requests/minute/IP by an in-memory limiter (lib/rate-limit.ts:3-4) and a per-email 5-attempt/15-minute lock (lib/auth.ts:9-10). title: Per-email lockout ledger has no aggregate cardinality bound or owner-side TTL: every distinct schema-valid email that fails once is retained indefinitely in process-global shared state
description: lib/auth.ts keeps an unbounded module-global Map loginAttempts (lib/auth.ts:12) keyed by attacker-chosen schema-valid emails. Reaching it pre-auth through the mounted NextAuth REST handler, any credential failure on a distinct email (unknown/missing-passwordHash/inactive account at lib/auth.ts:104-105, wrong password at :111-112) permanently retains one module-global entry ({count, lockedUntil}). No global sweep, timeout, or size cap exists anywhere in project source (repo-wide grep: only unrelated node_modules lru-cache matches in package-lock.json); the only deletions are a same-identifier delete-on-touch inside isLockedOut (:27-29) and clearAttempts on successful login (:44, invoked only at :117) — neither reachable for an email an attacker never retries and that never authenticates. Count<5 rows carry lockedUntil: 0, so no expiry is ever computed for them at all. Independently reproduced at commit 4337dfb457e4ceb2eba9b3abf17a695b5ac67c4d in the parent-approved sandbox on verbatim-extracted functions: 100,000 distinct emails -> 100,000 retained entries (~154 B each cumulative, 19.0 MB heapUsed) with zero evictions at every growth phase (10k/50k/100k), and expired-locked retention persisting >15 lock windows absent an identical-identifier retry; the hunter fixture reached the same invariant at 300,000 distinct emails. title: 5-failure login lockout cannot engage against sequential wrong-password attempts: isLockedOut deletes the {count, lockedUntil:0} sentinel written by every sub-threshold failure
description: recordFailedAttempt initializes a fresh failure entry as {count:0, lockedUntil:0} (lib/auth.ts:35) and only asserts lockedUntil when count reaches MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=5 (lib/auth.ts:37-39). isLockedOut (lib/auth.ts:27-29) treats lockedUntil=0 as already expired — Date.now() > 0 is always true — and deletes the retained entry, and authorize() executes that gate (lib/auth.ts:95) before every recordFailedAttempt call (lib/auth.ts:105/:112), with awaits at :100-102/:109 suspending between gate and record. Across strictly sequential wrong-password authorize() calls the counter therefore never exceeds 1 and the declared 5-failure/15-minute lock cannot engage: paced guessing is bounded only by the XFF-first-segment-keyed 10/min per-IP limiter (rate-limit map fingerprint owned by verifier-a, cited as a condition) and bcrypt cost latency; the 'Account locked due to many attempts' gate (lib/auth.ts:95-98) returns null only for genuinely posted locks. The state machine is not globally dead: when five authorize() executions overlap so that every gate runs before the first record continuation (concurrent submissions), the counter does reach 5, lockedUntil is posted, and subsequent serial attempts are answered 'locked' until the 15-minute expiry — independently verified — so the control fails precisely the paced credential-guessing shape it exists to stop, while still tripping on bursts.
root_cause: destructive interaction of two in-file constants/functions: the initializing sentinel {count:0, lockedUntil:0} in recordFailedAttempt (lib/auth.ts:35) versus isLockedOut's expiry predicate Date.now() > entry.lockedUntil (lib/auth.ts:27-29), under which lockedUntil=0 is always 'expired' and the background is the authorize() driver: the isLockedOut gate (:95) precedes every record path, and the awaited prisma findUnique (:100-102) and bcrypt.compare (:109) suspend between gate and record, so strictly sequential authorize() executions delete the retained {count:1, lockedUntil:0} sentinel on each next touch (the sync accessor methods themselves cannot interleave mid-function on Node's single-threaded event loop; only cross-request overlap at those await points escapes the deletion). The smallest effective fix in source is to make only real posted locks time-bound — e.g., treat lockedUntil>0 as the sole expiry predicate — so the count survives across authorize() calls and the threshold at lib/auth.ts:37 executes.
intended_behavior: five consecutive failed passwords on one email must set entry.lockedUntil at lib/auth.ts:38 to now+15min and force the next authorize() for that email to return null at lib/auth.ts:95-98 before touching prisma or bcrypt; once the lock expires the counter restarts; on success the account's entry is cleared (lib/auth.ts:117).

title: API rate limit is keyed on client-controlled X-Forwarded-For/x-real-ip into a process-lifetime unbounded Map: per-request key spoofing escapes the entire budget and grows server heap permanently
description: GET /api/news (unauthenticated — middleware.ts:49-51 matches only /admin/:path* and /api/admin/:path*) and the credentials login share one in-memory counter keyed by lib/rate-limit.ts#checkRateLimit on the raw string "x-forwarded-for" ?? "x-real-ip" ?? "unknown" (app/api/news/route.ts:11) or the first comma segment of x-forwarded-for (lib/auth.ts:18, used at :81). Any unseen key string instantiates a fresh full 10/60s budget (Map.set, count=1) with no cardinality cap, no aggregate dimension, and no eviction of expired entries; resetRateLimit (lib/rate-limit.ts:25) has zero call sites repo-wide. An attacker rotating a fresh header value per request escapes the intended per-IP budget entirely (observed 60/60 allowed for 60 distinct keys in one window), and unique keys are one Map entry each retained for the worker's lifetime (observed heap growth of ~23.7 MB per 200k keys persisting after every 60s window had expired and two forced GCs, ~124 bytes per retained key; ~49 MB rss retained). All headerless principals additionally collapse into the single shared 'unknown' bucket, exhaustible by one principal for 60s (which also gates their logins via the shared Map), and the two consumers parse the same header two different ways so identical requests occupy differently-partitioned buckets — no consumer's parse enforces a fixed trusted-ingress policy. Subsumes the peer alias lib/rate-limit.ts:6-22.attack-controlled-xff-key as the same root cause (same Map, same header-trust input); this one record is keyed to the primary fingerprint.
root_cause: lib/rate-limit.ts#checkRateLimit tunes per-key state on an attacker-controlled arbitrary-length string, with no key normalization/cap, no Map size bound, no expiration sweep, and no aggregate (global) dimension; callers feed it raw request headers (app/api/news/route.ts:11; lib/auth.ts:18).
intended_behavior: The limiter should key on an identity a client cannot freely nonce (a trusted-ingress-derived value), enforce one canonical parse across all consumers, bound the number and size of retained keys with eviction of expired entries, and keep a shared 'unknown'/'fallback' key from being a standing DoS handle on any surface.

title: Seed installs hardcoded default admin credentials (admin@bahianews.com.br / admin123) when ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD are unset or blank
description: prisma/seed.ts reads ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD with hardcoded fallbacks (admin@bahianews.com.br / admin123) and, when the resolved fallback email does not yet exist, hashes the fallback plaintext with bcrypt (declared cost 12) and creates a User row with role ADMIN (prisma/schema.prisma:138-141). The fallback is fail-open: unset AND empty-string configuration values both select the hardcoded credential (JS || falsy semantics), and there is no required-configuration guard, no generated secret, and no length/format validation before hashing. Verifier-i independently verified every traced/evidenced line at repo @ 4337dfb457e4ceb2eba9b3abf17a695b5ac67c4d (clean tree) and re-ran its own verbatim-extraction replay of seed.ts:7-27 under the parent-approved sandbox (env -i, unshare -U -r -n, bwrap --ro-bind / /, prlimit as=4GiB/nproc=128/fsize=64MiB, node --max-old-space-size=512, exit 0): unset env and blank-string env both select admin@bahianews.com.br/admin123 and take the create branch; provided values bypass the fallback; create-if-missing never resets an existing admin on re-run; exactly one ADMIN account (name 'Administrador') is created per run with bcrypt called at cost 12 on the fallback plaintext (bcryptjs stubbed — not importable here, no node_modules).
